newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak NBS says Oct M2 growth about 18pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Slovak NBS says Oct M2 growth about 18pct yr/yr.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) vice-governor Marian Jusko on Thursday told a conference the country's October key M2 money supply figure was "about 18 percent" higher, year-on-year.
Speaking at the same conference, Elena Kohutikova, the head of the NBS monetary department, said M2 growth is expected between 16 to 18 percent at the end of this year.

"Measures adopted by the NBS in July appeared to be bringing positive results. For example, M2 growth has been continuously slowing down since August and was at about 18 percent in October," Jusko told the conference in Bratislava.
Slovak M2 money rose 19.0 percent year-on-year in September, compared with a 19.5 percent rise in August.
Kohutikova told Reuters at the conference added that the central bank forecasts M2 growth to be under 18 percent at the end of the year.
"Despite an expected slight increase at the end of the year, we see M2 growth between 16 to 18 percent," she said.
The NBS had stated previously that its 1996 full-year target of an M2 expansion of 11.6 percent year-on-year.
"It is clear now that we will not reach the planned target," Jusko added.
The NBS implemented a series of measures in July aiming to tighten the money supply and curb inflation and the expansion of credit.

The moves included hikes in the last-resort lending facility, the Lombard rate and minimum reserve requirements for banks, which, together with a new NBS measure aimed at curbing domestic lending, gradually boosted interbank money market rates to around 15 percent.
